newsitem.title: HONG KONG: HK police fan out in search for illegal refugees.
newsitem.headline: HK police fan out in search for illegal refugees.

text.p: Hong Kong police fanned out across a rural outlying island on Monday searching for possibly hundreds of illegal Vietnamese immigrants.
Eleven boatpeople had been captured and authorities were continuing land, sea and air searches for the others, police said.
"The operation is still going on at the moment," a police spokesman said on Monday night.
Those captured told police they had been dropped off by a freighter on Sunday on Lantau, Hong Kong's largest island, and said 600 illegal immigrants were aboard the ship.
The latest batch of boatpeople left Quang Ninh in northern Vietnam 12 days ago, a local television station said.

Hong Kong, which was made a first asylum port by its former sovereign Britain, has been trying to repatriate or find third countries for tens of thousands of illegal Vietnamese immigrants in recent years.
Repatriation exercises became more frequent in the months approaching Hong Kong's reversion to Chinese rule on July 1 with Beijing demanding all camps be cleared by the handover.
More than 3,000 Vietnamese are still in the territory's detention camps, a legacy of the Vietnam War which ended in 1975 with the fall of the government of U.S.-backed Saigon to Hanoi's forces.
In the years that followed, hundreds of thousands left their homeland for countries around the region.
